# Independent audit of the all-dimensional simplex joint-row budget

Audited all six sections of `candidate bbd1a18ecbb9d3f0`. **PASS**, with one requested coefficient-rescaling wording repair in Section 6.

The strict distinct-vertex incidence gives the stated edge fractions and actual cap volume. The pyramid volume formula gives sigma_i=d|K|q_i/(H a_i), so inverse section weights are proportional to f_i/q_i^((d-1)/d), with the common normalization retained. The rowwise arithmetic-geometric mean and variance identity have the exact factors.

The group averaging fixes the selected index and simultaneously permutes rows and columns. It preserves the column sums. The selected-row average has B=(sum b_ij)/d; strict positivity of every other off-diagonal entry gives B<(1-A)/d, so C>0. The other averaged row has one channel exactly 1/d and d-1 channels exactly (1-A-B)/(d-1). These facts yield (6) with the displayed powers of d. Concavity of geometric mean follows from the given linear-infimum representation; applying it to each row and then summing compares the entire other-row sum, without making a false individual comparison. The final decreasing frontier gives the claimed inequality.

The nonnegative two-term deficit is exact. For equality, all positive vectors entering a geometric-mean average must be proportional, as follows from the unique optimizing supporting linear functional. The selected-row permutations have equal sums and hence equal entries. In each other row, permutations fixing that row and the selected index force all nonselected channels equal; proportionality between rows gives a common ratio. The column equations then force the actual common channel Q and P=1/d, precisely (8). This also works in d=2, where a row has only one nonselected channel. Conversely those conditions make all relevant averaged channel vectors identical.

For the sharp examples, the open A interval is nonempty exactly because x<d. It gives A,B,t,C>0. The actual vertex evaluation matrix agrees with the prescribed symmetric matrix. The edge matrix is (t+C)I+(A/d-C)11^T, with positive eigenvalues t+C and A+B, proving affine independence. The displayed positive barycentric coefficients sum to one and their vertex combination is zero. Thus the examples are genuine simplices with interior source and strict cap incidence for every x in (0,d).

The theorem is restricted to d>=2 and strict simplex incidences. The separate d=1 sentence avoids the undefined exponent and correctly has both one-channel values equal to one. No boundary-incidence limit, arbitrary-body extension, or lattice parity conclusion is inferred.

Requested prose repair: multiplying an ambient halfspace inequality by its positive circuit coefficient preserves that halfspace and every fiber trace, but the numerical integer coefficients are multiplied by the same factor. They should not be described as numerically unchanged. This does not affect the proof because every geometric halfspace remains exactly the same.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
